old_caption: The video captures a serene sunrise scene, where the sun is just beginning to rise above the horizon, casting a warm golden glow across the landscape. The sky is filled with a mix of fluffy white clouds and darker, more ominous ones, creating a dynamic and textured backdrop. In the foreground, bare trees stand silhouetted against the brightening sky, their branches reaching out into the air. To the left, tall electrical towers rise up, partially obscured by the misty atmosphere. The sun continues its ascent, illuminating the clouds with a soft light and gradually revealing more details of the landscape below. The overall mood of the video is peaceful and contemplative, capturing the quiet beauty of nature at dawn.

caption: The video captures a backlit landscape in which a bright sun sits just above a thick, glowing layer of ground fog. A leafless tree spreads its bare branches across the lower center, while darker trees line the bottom-right edge of the frame. To the left, two lattice electrical transmission towers rise out of the mist, the farther one fainter than the nearer. Above, scattered grey-white clouds hang across a sky that opens into a patch of blue in the upper right, and a small dark shape intrudes at the very top edge. Throughout the excerpt the sun, its glare, the cloud pattern, the fog, the trees, and the towers all hold the same positions and brightness. The camera viewpoint stays fixed, and no object displacement, deformation, or change in lighting is discernible.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
